document.title: Equipment certification review
document.subtitle: Fictional equipment review feature used to test a portable authoring package.
document.modelIntro: One submission owns the current decision. Immutable review events retain history across rejection and resubmission.
document.notStored: Equipment validity derives from APPROVED plus a future expiry date. Upload failures stay in client state. General booking eligibility is outside this sample.
document.flowContract: worker submit → certification service → atomic submission and event writes → worker and Ops projections
document.diagramNote: Worker identity reuse is source-backed. Certification service, permission and app layouts are proposed. Actions simulate the contract without backend calls.

decisions: The proposed certification service owns mutation commands.
Approval grants equipment validity only. Booking permission is evaluated separately.
Permission denial and expired certificates leave state unchanged.
Upload failure is visible and retryable; no event exists until successful submit.
questions: Should certificates expiring today remain valid through the facility-local day? This test requires a later date.
Which Ops role receives certification-review permission?
Which storage and retention policy should hold the certificate document?

flows.title: Submit, review and return a certificate
flows.summary: A submission reaches Ops. A decision reaches the worker; rejection permits edit and resubmission.
steps: Prepare
Worker enters number and expiry
Require complete fields and future facility-local expiry
No write until upload and submit succeed
Ready state or visible validation error
Submit
Worker sends content, request ID and revision
Authenticate owner; require DRAFT; check retry key
PENDING plus SUBMITTED event atomically
Ops sees the same certificate; worker sees Pending
Decide
Ops sends decision, reason, request ID and reviewed revision
Require permission, PENDING and matching revision; approval requires future expiry
APPROVED or REJECTED plus decision event atomically
Worker sees validity or rejection reason
Return or retry
Rejected worker edits; failed upload retries
Only REJECTED may edit; repeated committed request ID returns prior result
Edit returns DRAFT plus EDITED event; next successful submit owns its event
Worker resubmits; Ops sees new pending revision

tables.name: equipment_certification_submissions
tables.purpose: Current content and review state for one worker and equipment type.

fields.name: id
fields.rule: UUID-shaped application string, matching existing text ID storage.

fields.name: equipmentType
fields.rule: FORKLIFT in this test; backend enum owns supported values.

fields.name: certificateNumber
fields.rule: Required on submit; worker-owned certificate identifier.

fields.name: expiresOn
fields.rule: Local date; approval requires after the facility-local current date.

fields.name: status
fields.rule: DRAFT, PENDING, APPROVED or REJECTED. Backend owns transitions.

fields.name: revision
fields.rule: Starts at 1; increments on edit; review compares current revision.

fields.name: rejectionReason
fields.rule: Required when REJECTED; null after edit.

fields.name: submittedAt
fields.rule: Latest successful submit instant; null for an unsubmitted draft.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.rule: Latest content or state mutation instant.

constraints: UNIQUE(workerId, equipmentType) allows one current submission per type.
Only DRAFT submits, only PENDING decides, and only REJECTED returns to DRAFT.
Status and event commit atomically after revision and current-state comparison.
REJECTED requires a nonempty rejectionReason; other states require null.
tables.relationships: Worker 1 → many submissions. Submission 1 → many events. Worker deletion follows existing retention policy; no cascade proposed.

tables.name: equipment_certification_review_events
tables.purpose: Immutable history with one retry key per command.

fields.name: requestId
fields.rule: Unique retry identity; repeating it returns original result.

fields.name: actorSubject
fields.rule: Authenticated subject snapshot; permission resolves before writing. No uninspected actor table assumed.

constraints: Events are immutable and retained with their submission.
REJECTED requires nonempty reason; other actions require null.
tables.relationships: Every event belongs to one submission; a submission has any number of events.
